rules.statement: Add a secrets, settings, encryption-key or role operation for the management console as one endpoint and hook that takes a ManagementOwner, not as a separate endpoint, hook or tab per owner kind.
rules.why: Per-owner copies mean a fix, such as cache-tag isolation, reaches one owner and misses the others.
rules.check: Look for new endpoints, hooks or containers in managementApi or apps/mgmt containers that are named or duplicated per owner kind (platform, team, tenant, client, resource server) instead of taking a ManagementOwner.

rules.statement: Build a management API path with ownerApiPath and its cache tags with the owner tag helpers, never by concatenating ids or deriving an API prefix from a scope by hand.
rules.why: The helpers hold the scope rules and URI-encoding of ids once; a hand-built path or tag can name the wrong route or collide with another owner's tag.
rules.check: Look for template strings like `api/teams/${...}` or hand-built tag ids in endpoints or callers instead of ownerApiPath, ownerTagId, ownerEffectiveTagId, ownerLimitsTagId or roleListTagId.

rules.statement: Address a client, resource server or scope endpoint and page through a tenantId under /api/tenants/{tenantId}, never through a platform or team scope, except listMachineClients and createMachineClient which take a MachineClientOwner.
rules.why: The API serves those operations only under the tenant route, so a platform or team address returns 404 and a type that accepts it hides the mistake until run time.
rules.check: Look for client or resource-server endpoints or pages that accept a ManagementScope or build a platform/team path, or a client detail page that does not use client.tenantId.

rules.statement: Type an owner-generic operation's parameter with the narrowest derived owner type the API supports (such as ClientOwner for rotateSecret, SecretOwner, EncryptionKeyOwner), not with ManagementOwner, so an unsupported owner fails to type-check.
rules.why: Secret rotation exists only for clients and other operations only for some owners; selecting by type makes the type checker refuse calls the API would reject.
rules.check: Look for endpoints or containers that accept ManagementOwner for an operation the API maps only for some owners, or that offer rotation for a non-client owner.

rules.statement: URI-encode every id embedded in a client-side cache tag and scope the tag to its owner, so that a mutation invalidates only its own owner's cached data.
rules.why: Unencoded ids containing a separator such as ':' can collide, letting one owner's mutation invalidate or leak into another owner's caches.
rules.check: Look for cache tag ids built from raw ids without encodeURIComponent, or tags not keyed by the owner's scope.
